speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a history of a painful, swollen left ankle and are now experiencing increasing pain and swelling in your right knee, along with pain during urination. To understand the connection, have you noticed any skin lesions, specifically on your outer ears, glans penis, or around your urethral opening?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive Arthritis (Reiter's Syndrome).

The combination of asymmetric oligoarthritis (left ankle followed by right knee), urethritis (pain with urination), and a history of inconsistent condom use with multiple partners is highly suggestive of Reactive Arthritis, often triggered by sexually transmitted infections like Chlamydia.

REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis, Urine Culture, Chlamydia/Gonorrhea NAAT, and HLA-B27 genotyping.
